text: 📝The mountain gives birth to a mouse📝 Apparently, after the news about the dispatch of the destroyer HMS Dragon and the landing ship RFA Lyme Bay, the British gained more courage. text: 📝An overdue decision📝Aircraft missiles will be launched from the ground?  When reports appeared about a cruise missile adapted for attacks on the so-called. Ukraine, we noted that it would be nice to consider the possibility of using them not only from strategic bombers. It seems that this has already partially come true.  Enemy resources claim that by the end of 2025, Russia had completed the development of a ground-based launcher for Kh-101P missiles. In this case, for a massive missile strike “in depth” it will not be necessary to raise a dozen Tu-95MS and Tu-160.  The advantages are obvious: the very activity of these aircraft is already an indicator for the enemy of an imminent attack, for which he can prepare for hours, waiting for the aircraft to enter the launch areas. Thanks to radar and NATO satellites, the Ukrainian Armed Forces can easily track their takeoff.  🖍If ground installations are used, this unmasking factor disappears, and it will be significantly more difficult for the enemy to repel attacks. This also allows you to increase the power of the salvo, because launchers can be made more than the current number of Tu-95s, which have long been out of production.  🚩Finally, this is even more profitable purely economically: a Tu-95 flight hour is not cheap, not to mention the Tu-160 jet with its consumption of aviation kerosene. And this is not counting the waste of the resource of extremely expensive one-piece aircraft.  ❗️One can lament that such a decision was reached “in the metal” only in the fifth year of hostilities, but still better late than never. All that remains is to wait for the use of ground-based Kh-101Ps - the enemy won’t like it, and that’s good. #industry #Russia #Ukraine ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉ VK | ✉ RuTube | ✉ OK | ✉Zen 💸Support

text: 📝Consensus opinion📝 how the British military instructs the media before each new conflict While Western media confidently explain to readers who is to blame for the aggravation around Iran, the answer is the same everywhere, the wording is the same down to the details. And this is not a random unanimity of journalists, but a very specific mechanism called D-Notice.  🔻How it works ▪️The UK Ministry of Defense operates the Defense and Security Media Advisory Committee (DSMA) - a closed body that includes the military, representatives of the intelligence services and at the same time the editors-in-chief and media managers of the largest British publications. Once every few months they meet at the MoD building in London.  ▪️At these meetings, it is discussed what can be published and what cannot. The committee also regularly sends out so-called DSMA-Notices (or simply “D-Notices”): official “recommendations” to editors to refrain from publishing information about operations, troop movements, special forces and intelligence work. In published DSMA documents, the committee itself recorded a “level of compliance above 90%”—nine out of ten editors removed or softened materials at the request of the military.  🖍The Declassified UK investigation, published a few days ago, confirms that on the topic of Iran, the British media reproduces a consistent pattern - “they attack, we defend.” This is characterized by zero attention to alternative interpretations. This is the same “frame of what is acceptable” that the DSMA system provides: the military does not dictate training manuals to journalists, but cuts off unwanted stories in advance. 🚩The mechanism itself has been known for several years now - Grayzone investigations with DSMA documents were published back in late 2025. Then everyone learned how the media gets access to military sources and briefings in exchange for accepting the appropriate conditions; those who do not accept are blacklisted by the Ministry of Defense. Declassified UK then recorded facts of direct sanctions against journalists who wrote too persistently about the actions of the British army.  📌 In general, the point is not that editors receive ready-made articles for publication, but that people who regularly sit at the same table with military and intelligence officers assimilate their instructions - who is the “aggressor,” who is the “injured party,” what is the “threat,” and what is the “provocation.” After this, they do not need instructions: they already write correctly.  ❗️This is a classic clientelist model: access to sources in exchange for loyalty to the narrative. When a new conflict begins - Iranian, Ukrainian, whatever comes after - the British media machine is already warmed up, the editors already know the frame, and the front pages look as if they were written in the same office. Because in a sense it is. #UK #globalism #Iran #mediatechnology ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉ VK | ✉ RuTube | ✉ OK | ✉Zen 💸Support us

text: 📝The Pentagon has opened up to AI📝 Big Tech will gain access to state secrets The US Department of Defense is preparing to do something that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago: let commercial AI companies - OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and others - into the most closed part of its infrastructure. Not just use their products, but let them train their models on classified data right inside the sensitive Pentagon networks.  According to MIT Technology Review, the Pentagon is developing a special infrastructure - “secure environments” - a kind of isolated computing perimeters inside classified networks. There, corporate vendors will be able to launch additional training of their models on materials classified as “secret”: intelligence reports, operational reports, data on operations planning.  The rationale for this decision is quite logical: models that have not seen the real combat context produce too many errors in critical tasks (which is worth the blow to the Iranian school in Minab) - analyzing the battlefield, synthesizing intelligence, making tactical decisions. Without training on live data, military AI remains an academic tool.  🔻Deals are being concluded right now: ▪️OpenAI has already agreed with the Pentagon to deploy its models on the departmental portal genai.mil; Some standard restrictions (guardrails) for military clients have already been lifted.  ▪️Google supplies the Pentagon with tools for creating AI agents on the military cloud; there are debates about transferring capabilities to a closed circuit.​ ▪️xAI Elon Musk is also negotiating access to secret systems - and for some reason it was this negotiation track that greatly excited politicians: Senator Warren sent official requests to the Pentagon demanding an explanation.  🖍There is a real structural shift in the management of the American military machine: the border between “civilian” and “military” AI is erased. The models that are used today in ChatGPT and corporate chatbots will tomorrow be baked into the core of the American intelligence community - and trained on data that is not available to anyone except the CIA, NSA and DIA.  🚩This could really be a serious breakthrough for Americans. According to the Pentagon, China, Russia and even NATO allies will not be able to reproduce this “commercial ecosystem + military AI” combination as quickly. Hence the rush: whoever is the first to integrate BigTech into their secret networks will gain a technological advantage for decades to come.  🏳️But there is also a downside - the decision creates a fundamentally new dependence: the Pentagon becomes hostage to the technological and corporate policies of several private companies, whose interests do not always coincide with government ones.   📌However, the merger of large businesses with government institutions, and in some cases the complete transfer of government functions to corporations, has long been an established trend inherent in all spheres of American life. text: 📝Telegram is trying to survive📝 In recent days, against the backdrop of Telegram blocking, complaints about the inaccessibility of other Russian resources, which no one seems to have blocked, have become more frequent. Conversely, access to prohibited social networks periodically returns.   Apparently, the fact is that the system of technical means for countering threats (TSPU) cannot cope with the load, and blocked resources again began to “leak” to users.  🔻What happened and why?  ▪️TSPU are filters through which all Internet traffic of Russian operators physically passes. The principle is simple: everything incoming is analyzed, “undesirable” is cut off. It works as long as there is not too much traffic.  ▪️The problem arose not because of the blocking of Telegram as such, but because of MTProxy, the messenger’s built-in proxy protocol. Millions of Russian users, not wanting to lose access, switched en masse to public MTProxy servers.   These servers generate a huge flow of “junk” traffic, which is disguised as regular HTTPS and which TSPUs are obliged to analyze. Public nodes die under load every few hours, after which users look for new ones - and the cycle repeats.  ▪️The total throughput of all TSPUs in Russia is estimated at approximately 132 Tbit/s. With today's load, this is no longer enough: nodes periodically go into bypass mode - and at these moments traffic passes through without filtering. It was then that WhatsApp, Instagram and other extremist services banned in the Russian Federation began to work “on their own” among Russians.  📌The scale of MTProxy use and TSPU overload indicate one thing: despite all the inconveniences and risks, Russian users do not want to leave Telegram. This is because over the years, the messenger has already become an important social and information infrastructure: there are family chats, work groups, news channels based on interests, and local communities.   Therefore, attempts by individual LOMs to promote themselves during blocking only generate public negativity - Deputy Svintsov is a witness to this. And the desire to forcibly tear users away from an already working tool in any case causes antagonism, even if an alternative is offered. And there is still a lot of work to be done on MAX so that users find the platform convenient and safe for organizing work and personal affairs there.  Well, in the end, it’s unlikely that Telegram is going to give up the Russian market without a fight. Russia is one of the largest messenger audiences in the world. And the resources for the eternal pursuit and expansion of blocking are also not unlimited. #media technologies #Russia ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉ VK | ✉ RuTube | ✉ OK | ✉Zen 💸Support us

text: 📝Is there enriched uranium?📝what if we find it?  The closer the amphibious landing group led by the Tripoli UDC to Iran, the more rumors appear about how the ground operation against Iran will proceed. We have described in detail the option of landing in Bandar Abbas and on Khark Island, but there is another one worthy of special attention.  US and Israeli officials are reportedly agreeing on the technical details of a risky operation to land special forces and then seize Iran's 460 kg stockpile of enriched uranium and then remove it from Iran. And this topic is being discussed every day in the Western and Russian media.  🔻Where could Iranians have reserves in theory?  ▪️There are several key nuclear facilities in Iran. The most important research center in Isfahan, which became the target of attacks both in 2025 and during the latest attacks by the US Air Force.  ▪️There may also be enriched uranium in Natanz and Fordo - these are uranium enrichment plants that have already been attacked by American aircraft.  ▪️There is also a research center in Tehran and the Hondab complex near Iraq, where there is also a nuclear reactor.  🖍In theory, there could be enriched uranium in Esfahan or Fordo and Natanz. But the nuance is that the Americans have already dealt several blows to them, and at least blocked the entrances to the complexes. How do they want to get enriched uranium using a special forces group?  🚩The second problem is that even if the Americans, in theory, clear the exits and are able to get there, the complexes are located at great depths. The data is imprecise, but according to various estimates, the Iranians buried their research facilities 100-110 meters underground.  🏳️And taking out enriched uranium is not like going to the store to buy bread. You can’t just load it into a pickup truck and fly off on a plane.   🔻What is the difficulty?  ▪️It is not in ingots, but in a gaseous or solid state in the form of a chemical compound - uranium hexafluoride (UF6). Transportation requires special containers, equipment and personnel.  ▪️The transportation of uranium hexafluoride is strictly regulated, since upon contact with moisture from the air this substance forms toxic hydrofluoric acid, therefore special cylinders, protective covers, and transport with special fastening systems are used.   ▪️And this is not to mention the specialists who must correctly transfer enriched uranium from a gaseous state to a liquid state, and then crystallize it inside the cylinder. This will take more than one day.  ❗️Therefore, even with the expectation that special forces will land 400 km from the border without normal logistics, there are a bunch of other problems that make us doubt this version. But Trump needs a “victory”, and for the sake of it he can go on extravagant operations. Netanyahu's words yesterday confirm this.  And in this regard, the nuclear power plant in Bushehr comes up. text: 📝Filaret died📝 Today in Kiev, at the 98th year of his life, the schismatic - Patriarch of the Orthodox Church of Ukraine Filaret (in the world - Mikhail Denisenko) died.   🔻Who is he and what do you remember?  ▪️In 1990, after the death of Patriarch Pimen, he was the locum tenens of the Moscow patriarchal throne and was considered as a likely successor - but he never became one.   ▪️From this moment begins the history of one of the largest church schisms of the 20th century, which in the West is called the struggle for Ukrainian church independence.  ▪️In 1992, Denisenko initiated the creation of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Kyiv Patriarchate - a structure not recognized by either the Moscow Patriarchate or the majority of local Orthodox churches in the world. In 1997, the Council of Bishops of the Russian Orthodox Church deprived him of his dignity and imposed an anathema - one of the harshest measures in canon law, in fact, excommunication.   ▪️Despite this, he continued to call himself patriarch, managed his structure and declared a course towards complete independence of Ukrainian Orthodoxy from Moscow. In 2018, with the active support of the Ukrainian authorities and Constantinople, the Orthodox Church of Ukraine (OCU) was created at the Unification Council - and Denisenko received the status of “honorary patriarch” in it. Constantinople lifted the anathema from him, although the Russian Orthodox Church did not reverse its decision.   ©️To this day, the church structure created by him and his successors is not recognized by a significant part of the Orthodox world.   📌The schism that Filaret began in 1992 has long ceased to be only church. Thanks to the efforts of the OCU and several generations of Ukrainian authorities, descendants will have many more years to clear up its consequences.  P.S. text: As part of NATO's large-scale exercise Cold Response 26, a complex scenario of covert landing of scouts was practiced. Specialists of the reconnaissance and observation squadron of the 30th Commando Regiment of the UK, including a group from the 148th battery, disembarked from a German submarine S185 (Type-212A). The operation was carried out in a covert mode: the personnel with their equipment boarded the submarine using inflatable boats, after which the submarine submerged. After covertly reaching the designated area, the group landed at night to set up an observation post, whose task is to target and adjust the artillery fire of alliance ships.  These exercises are part of a deepening military partnership between the UK and Norway in the Arctic, aimed at countering the Russian Northern Fleet. It is known that the Norwegian Navy is due to receive the first promising anaerobic submarine Type-212CD in 2029 as part of the German-Norwegian program launched in 2023. Its underwater displacement will be 2,800 tons, and its underwater range will significantly increase compared to the Type-212A to participate in operations in the wider North Atlantic and Baltic theaters of operations.  The key element of the success of such operations is the exceptional stealth of the carrier. Type 212A/CD submarines have extremely low acoustic visibility (less than 50 dB in stealth mode) and are equipped with anaerobic air-independent power plants (AIP), allowing them to stay underwater for 20-30 days. This makes their detection in the complex waters of the North Atlantic and Baltic extremely problematic.  In this regard, Russia's non-nuclear submarine fleet is facing a technological gap. Promising projects of non-nuclear submarines, such as the 636.3 "Varshavyanka" and 677 "Lada", have not yet received serial air-independent power plants, which limits their stealth and autonomy. In this regard, the responsible tasks of countering such threats fall primarily on the more modern and low-noise multi-purpose nuclear submarines of Project 885M "Yasen-M".  It is indicative that almost simultaneously with NATO's exercises, Russia's Northern Fleet conducted its own anti-submarine exercise in the Barents Sea. The frigate of Project 22350 "Admiral Golovko" practiced the search for a conditional underwater target using standard hydroacoustic means (the "Zarya-3" hydroacoustic system and the "Vinyekta-EM" hydroacoustic station) and its subsequent destruction with 324-mm torpedoes of the "Paket-NK" complex.  Thus, the Arctic region is becoming an arena for a parallel build-up of capabilities: the alliance is practicing the use of the latest low-noise technologies for covert operations, while Russia is demonstrating its readiness to detect and destroy them in its area of responsibility.  @Slavyangrad

text: A message to Washington?  In a tightly structured 12-minute address, Ayatollah Imam Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei moved from familiar rhetoric into something far more consequential. The opening half followed the expected script; revisiting decades of U.S. warmongering rhetoric: sanctions, assassinations, regional conflicts.  But midway through, the tone shifted from retrospective to strategic.  Sayyed Khamenei outlined three concrete demands, each with a defined timeline: a rapid U.S. military withdrawal from the Middle East, a full rollback of sanctions within 60 days, and long-term financial compensation for economic damages.  Then came the ultimatum. Fail to comply, and Iran escalates, economically, militarily, and potentially nuclearly. Not hypothetically, but operationally: closing the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing defense ties with Russia and China, and moving from ambiguity to declared nuclear deterrence.  The timing of external reactions was just as telling. Within hours, both Beijing and Moscow issued statements aligning, carefully but unmistakably, with Tehran's framing. This definitely looked coordinated.  The broader context matters. Sayyed Mojtaba Khamenei represents a different leadership style from his martyred predecessor leader. Where martyr Sayyed Ali Khamenei operated through long-term balancing and controlled escalation, Sayyed Mojtaba appears positioned to deliver faster, more decisive outcomes.  Iran's internal reports are clear, the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps is in no way, shape or form interested in incrementalism. They are pushing for structural change: removing U.S. influence from the region, restoring Iran's military standing, and forcing a re-negotiation of global power dynamics.  And for the first time in decades, Iran practically has the leverage to  do this.  Rising oil prices, regional instability, growing alignment with China and Russia, and vulnerabilities in global trade routes have shifted the strategic landscape.  So this was not just a speech. It was a test. A test of whether the United States is willing, or even able, to operate under a new set of constraints.  What happens next will likely define not just the trajectory of this conflict, but the broader balance of power in the Middle East for decades to come.

The last one was Giles Dooley, a documentary photographer and founder of a charitable organization that, in particular, donates ambulances to Ukraine. World media about the war on March 16 🖌About how Ukrainian technologies for combating drones are beginning to be in increasing demand in the world, writes NBC News. The long war forced Ukraine to constantly test new drone technologies directly on the battlefield. It is thanks to this that a unique system of rapid improvement of drones was formed in the country, said Marko Kushnir, the spokesman of one of the leading Ukrainian drone manufacturers General Chereshnya. "We can get feedback from the military in the morning and come up with a solution in the evening that will help with new tasks on the battlefield," he says.   Now there is a great demand for this experience from other countries: private organizations and governments in the Middle East have already turned to "General Chereshny" for help. That help will include not only the sale of drones, but also the supporting infrastructure they need, such as batteries and maintenance protocols, and most importantly, the experience of using them, Kushnir said.  The attitude of the United States has also changed: back in the summer, a Ukrainian delegation offered the Americans their experience in combating drones, but they became sharply interested in it only after the war with Iran began, said a European official familiar with the matter.  🖌Trump's war with Iran has started a vicious circle: Europe is now indirectly financing Putin's war against Ukraine — and at the same time protecting it. This is stated in an editorial column by Benjamin Bidder for Der Spiegel. The shock of oil prices is a kind of rejuvenating treatment for the "most dangerous adversary of the continent" Vladimir Putin, writes the author of the column. According to him, before the start of the war in the Middle East, the Russian economy had already begun to weaken: revenues from oil and gas fell, budget revenues decreased, large companies were overloaded with debts, and Russia was thinking about reducing public spending.    But now all this can be wasted, because the price of oil has risen - the Russian Urals in some places is even more expensive than Brent. The author of the column claims that Moscow is already receiving billions in additional profits from this situation, and if prices remain high for a long time, Russia will be able to earn approximately $10 billion more every month. This will create a double financial burden for Europe. On the one hand, the rise in global energy prices means more expensive fuel and energy for European economies, which increases Russia's income from oil exports. On the other hand, if Putin's oil revenues continue to grow, so will his ability to wage war against Ukraine — and the European aid package for Ukraine will be exhausted sooner than Brussels expects. Then it is likely that even more funds will be needed for Kyiv soon.  🗞This is only part of the review. text: 📚📖Despite the chronic shortage of infantry, Ukraine can still conduct successful offensive operations. World media about the war on March 17 🖌Ukraine is currently developing its own air defense system, similar to the Israeli "Iron Dome", says El Pais. The main problem is that the territory of Ukraine is about 30 times larger than that of Israel, so creating such a shield is much more difficult. This system should combine radars, anti-aircraft missiles, electronic warfare and interceptor drones, the article says. But the Ukrainian shield must be adapted to the country's own capabilities and cannot rely solely on expensive Western air defense systems such as Patriot or IRIS-T. "Our task is to build an anti-drone dome over Ukraine: a system that does not react after the fact, but destroys the threat as it approaches," Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said in January.   🖌Financial Times publishes an article about the successes of the Ukrainian offensive at the front over the last month, despite the relatively small number of infantry. Ukrainian paratroopers and assault units advanced in the southeast — in the Zaporizhzhya and Dnipropetrovsk regions, and liberated several settlements. Last week, after a trip to the east, Volodymyr Zelenskyi said that Ukraine had recaptured approximately 400-435 sq. km of territory. Independent analysts give lower estimates and say that Kyiv may exaggerate some of the numbers, the publication notes. But they agree that the Ukrainian operation, which began at the beginning of February, really signals a real ability to repel Russian troops.  Several factors contributed to this at once: better planning of operations, use of elite units, mass use of drones, drone strikes on Russian equipment and logistics. Given this, there is every reason to believe that it may be more difficult for Russia to advance in 2026 than it was last year, says military analyst Rob Lee of the Institute for Foreign Policy Studies. But the coming months will not be easy for Kyiv either — the arrival of spring means the return of vegetation along the entire front line, which Russian assault groups use to hide from reconnaissance drones and advance deep into Ukrainian lines. In addition, Russian troops have almost captured Pokrovsk and Gulyaipole and are approaching Kramatorsk and Slovyansk, FT writes.  🗞This is only part of the review. text: 📚📖 European allies can exchange protection of the Strait of Hormuz for help to Ukraine. World media about the war on March 18 🖌About a possible diplomatic agreement between the USA and Europe, which could simultaneously help solve two international crises - Russia's war against Ukraine and Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which almost 20% of the world's oil supplies pass, writes Forbes. With the strait blocked, energy prices have skyrocketed, supplies have become more difficult, and political instability could spread from the Middle East to Europe and Asia, and eventually to the United States. Therefore, the strait should be opened as soon as possible, and the US needs the help of allies, the article says.   The representative of the World Food Program of the United Nations Karl Skau warned: if the war in the Middle East continues until June, another 45 million people could be on the brink of acute hunger due to rising prices. Food shortages will force people to leave their homes. Migration will increase political tensions, and this affects elections, alliances and security policy - primarily in Europe, but also in the US. Therefore, Donald Trump should seriously consider the idea of ​​the President of Finland, Alexander Stubb: Europe will help with the security of the Strait of Hormuz, in return, the United States will promise long-term support to Ukraine. It looks like a transactional agreement and that is why it can work, writes the publication. Trump has long viewed foreign policy as deals rather than doctrines. He called on allies to make more contributions, and he was not too interested in commitments without an expiration date. As the publication writes, such an agreement can be beneficial for both the US and Europe, as it will allow for the distribution of responsibility among the allies and at the same time stabilize the energy situation in the world and strengthen Russia's deterrence.  🗞This is only part of the review. text: 📚📖Ukraine preserved the operation of sea ports during the war - this is what the Persian Gulf countries want to learn. World media about the war on March 19 🖌Despite the blockade of the Black Sea, shelling, mine danger and cyberattacks, Ukraine was able to preserve the operation of its sea ports during the war - now this experience is being carefully studied by other countries, writes Der Spiegel. Against the backdrop of Iran's blockade of oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, port operators in the Persian Gulf countries are trying to understand how Ukraine managed to survive such a blockade and resume maritime trade. "The experience we gained in Ukraine has no analogues," says the head of the Association of Ukrainian Ports, Dmytro Barinov, after speaking to members of the International Association of Ports and Harbors in Odesa.   At first, the Ukrainian military pushed the Russian fleet away from the coast and took control of part of the Black Sea. After that, they launched their own sea corridor closer to the shore — ships with grain went through it, says Barinov. Ports began to work according to a clear schedule: ships enter and leave only at certain times. The military inspects ships while still at sea. Суднам не дозволяють довго стояти в очікуванні — це занадто небезпечно. In the sea, floating barriers were installed that catch mines, and on the territory of the ports - mobile concrete shelters, where workers go in case of alarms. Ports constantly coordinate work with air defense units. After the hacker attacks, part of the processes were transferred to faxes in order not to depend on digital systems.  🖌The biggest threat to Europe right now is Russia and the war against Ukraine, says former NATO Secretary General George Robertson, who headed the Alliance from 1999 to 2003, in an interview with the Finnish public broadcaster Yle. According to him, the support of Kyiv should be the main priority of the Alliance, and if the West is distracted by other crises, in particular in the Middle East, it may have dangerous consequences for the whole of Europe. Ukraine needs more weapons and wider support, and Russia needs to be clearly shown that it cannot win, Robertson notes. text: People's deputy Volodymyr Aryev wrote that former political prisoner Volodymyr Balukh was beaten in the TCC. The situation is being investigated by the police, and the TCC denies all accusations.  According to Aryev, Balukh, who has a disability of the II group, was taken to the TCC on March 19 after the trial of Roman Chervinsky due to an incorrectly registered disability. He claims that the former political prisoner was beaten on the head in the premises of the TCC, and then kept in handcuffs all night.   The Kyiv TCC confirmed that Balukh was taken to the premises of the center for violation of military records. They say that there was no information about his stay in captivity in the registers, and he did not have the right to a reprieve, so he was sent to the VLK.  In the end, the information that he has a disability was obtained from other registers, but Balukh, as they say in the TCC, did not issue a deferment. He was served with a summons requiring him to update his data and released. The TCC assures that the veteran was not beaten or kept in handcuffs, and he himself did not write any complaints.  Meanwhile, the Kyiv police reported that they were checking the information about the beating of Balukh, who is currently in the hospital. Police were sent to the hospital to take a statement.  Balukh himself said in a comment to "Suspilne Krym" that he had a bruise on his chest and shoulder.   "The prosecutor filed an application against me in the Chervinskyi case - allegedly I insulted him with obscene language, and I was invited to give an explanation in the Pechersk District Department. I arrived, gave an explanation, and after that at the exit, literally two meters away, there was a bus - they pushed me into it and took me to the TCC, saying that I was allegedly wanted. text: 📚📖 "Orban has beaten the EU again - and maybe for the last time." World media about the Russian-Ukrainian war March 20 🖌"The city is sleeping. Defense forces combine various elements of protection: early detection of targets using a network of sensors and artificial intelligence to destroy them at different stages - in the air, on the approach to the city and already directly above the objects. Ukraine's experience in countering Russia's massive shelling — often larger than what Iran has so far carried out in the Persian Gulf — means it has something to offer the West in exchange for aid, the article says. "The trajectory of our interceptions is improving," says Commander Dmytro Pletenchuk, spokesman for the Ukrainian Navy. "The share of downed planes often reaches 90%."  🖌Viktor Orban outwitted the EU again and blocked a €90 billion loan for Ukraine. Despite 16 years of participation in European summits, this meeting may be his last, writes Politico. As the publication notes, Orban has been annoying Brussels for a long time, along with Paris, Berlin and other capitals. Before the meeting of the European Council, the EU prepared a compromise that would allow the Hungarian prime minister to save face during the election campaign and at the same time agree to a loan. It was about delaying the allocation of funds to Kyiv until the supply of Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline is restored. "You have to treat Orbán like a six-year-old child, adapt to him," one diplomat told Politico.   If Orbán is re-elected — which one EU official said many leaders in the summit hall thought likely — then he may be more willing to approve the loan once oil is flowing again through the Druzhba pipeline. But if he does not do this, Hungary may be punished at the next meeting of EU leaders in Cyprus on April 23-24. author: SuspilneNews
text: Today, the Orthodox Church of Ukraine announced the death of the Honorary Patriarch of Kyiv and All Russia-Ukraine Filaret. He died at the age of 97 from exacerbation of chronic diseases. Filaret devoted 81 years of his life to the church.  Metropolitan Epiphany, the head of the OCU, wrote that the patriarch did a lot to preserve church life both during the years of Soviet oppression and during the struggle for the establishment of church autocephaly.  This struggle was difficult and dramatic. In order to recognize the independence of Ukrainian Orthodoxy, he agreed to liquidate the church he had been building for over 20 years. Voluntarily giving up power, Filaret could not accept that he did not return it.   The article tells about the path of one of the key Orthodox figures of independent Ukraine.

text: Sociologist on the "Budanov phenomenon" and the expectations of Ukrainians: "The military should come to power" The head of the "Rating" sociological group, Oleksiy Antipovich, connects the growth of the government's ratings with the so-called "Budanov phenomenon". The basis of this phenomenon is the colossal credit of public trust in the military, because 80% of citizens are convinced that they should be involved in the management of the country and hold public positions. The expert reported this in an interview with Deutsche Welle.  "80% of Ukrainians say that the military should participate in the elections. The military should come to power, the military should head state positions in Ukraine," the sociologist notes.  At the same time, Antipovich emphasizes the fact that changing the strict military hierarchy to a civilian model of management requires a certain transformation.  "Can a military man, or a professional military man, be the prime minister? Question. After all, it is necessary to understand the economy, it is necessary to manage somehow not directively, but to manage some kind of state mechanism, in which there are a lot of ministries, some lines, the Verkhovna Rada, some committees, laws. This is not vertical, which a military man carries out on orders," Oleksiy Antipovich explains.  Therefore, the high level of support for the military, and in particular for Kyryll Budanov, reflects the request of Ukrainians for "strong leadership" during the war. However, integrating a military style of governance into a civilian system is a unique challenge that requires a thoughtful approach and adaptation.

text: The Budanov phenomenon: Ukrainians want to see the military in power The appointment of Kyril Budanov to the post of head of the President's Office was not just a personnel rotation, but a real "social tranquilizer" for the country. This decision directly correlates with the large-scale request of Ukrainian society for the presence of the military in power structures.  Currently, about 80% of citizens express a desire to see representatives of the army in public positions. Since this personnel decision met people's expectations, it quite naturally transformed into high ratings of support and trust in Budanov himself.  Political scientists explain the phenomenon of growing trust in people with combat experience by the fact that Ukrainians see them as a guarantee of security and protection, as well as the potential for effective state management.  "Ukrainian society looks for support in those who give a sense of security. And the military, following the example of Budanov, will naturally continue to be the bearers of this trust. This trend can significantly affect the formation of the future political landscape of Ukraine. At the same time, the main challenge remains the ability of the state to effectively integrate the military into civilian management processes," concluded blogger Mykhailo Shnayder.

text: 🇺🇦🇫🇷 LITKOVSKA conquered Paris Fashion Week with a collection about the indomitable Kyiv this winter.  The Ukrainian brand entered the main schedule of Paris Fashion Week for the first time, presenting the Autumn–Winter 2026/27 collection called FIREFLY.  According to designer Lilia Litkovska, the collection was inspired by winter Kyiv during blackouts.  “In Kyiv, there are days without electricity, without heat, without water. People move around the city with small flashlights on their heads. From afar, the streets resemble a sky that has fallen to the ground — scattered with moving tiny stars, fireflies. It was this image that became the soul of the collection.  FIREFLY explores the idea of an inner light that does not fade under the pressure of circumstances and unites people even in times of uncertainty,” Litkovska shared.  This image became the central idea of the show — an inner light that does not go out even in the dark.  A special feature of the presentation was a fragrance created together with a perfumer, designed to convey the smell of winter Kyiv — cold air, stone, smoke, and human presence.  Throughout the show, the flashlight appears both as a practical object and as a metaphor for direction and survival.  “When there is darkness around, one light helps another find the way,” the brand representatives added.

text: North Korea earned between $7.67 billion and $14.4 billion from sending troops and weapons to the Russian Federation, according to a report by the Institute for National Security Strategy of South Korea.  The report states that the amount of foreign currency received from the four waves of troop deployments is estimated at $620 million.  The amount of foreign currency received from exporting various artillery systems, shells, and ballistic missiles between August 2023 and December 2025 is estimated at $7.05–13.78 billion.  A significant part (80–96%) of the compensation was or will be received in the form of sensitive military technologies, precision components, and related materials.  The report says that if North Korea receives the full amount for troop deployments and arms exports, the main economic effect of sanctions against the DPRK — a reduction in foreign currency revenues — would be neutralized.  It predicts that, if cooperation continues, North Korea could earn $560 million annually from troop deployments alone. However, the confirmed compensation received so far is estimated at about 4–19.6% of the projected income.  According to the British Open Source Centre and the Russian media outlet Important Stories, since the summer of 2023, four Russian ships have made at least 112 trips to the DPRK, delivering between 8 and 11 million rounds of ammunition to the Russian Federation.  On average, Russia received about 350,000 rounds per month, allowing it to maintain the pace of offensive operations.  The companies “MG-Flot” and “Sovfrakht” were involved in supplies from the DPRK. The owner of 50% of MG-Flot shares, Jamaldin Pashayev, is under US sanctions for importing drone components from Iran to Russia.

One such drone is about 40 times cheaper than a Patriot missile. In terms of production time and cost, it is impossible to compete with drones. There simply will not be enough resources.  In the long term, drones have no distance limits. Today they fly 100 km, tomorrow 1,000, and the day after tomorrow 10,000. That is why modern defense must be developed.  Today, Ukraine is number one in these technologies, and the United States has the most effective and powerful army in the world. If we are talking about an exchange — a real exchange of security, guarantees, and experience — we are open. This is a real partnership offer.  An interceptor drone costs $3,000–5,000. One Shahed costs about $10,000, while a Patriot missile costs $4 million. Ukraine spends about $10,000 to shoot down a drone, while a Middle Eastern country spends $4 million. This is the experience we offer.”

author: United24Media
text: All regions of Russia are now under threat of Ukrainian drone strikes, said Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu at an off-site meeting in Yekaterinburg.  According to him, until recently the Urals were out of reach of strikes from Ukrainian territory, but are now under immediate threat.  Shoigu noted that the Urals are home to strategic defense industry enterprises, as well as energy and chemical facilities, major oil and gas fields, key railway lines, and important highways.  “Disabling them could not only cause significant economic damage but also destabilize the functioning of large metropolitan areas and disrupt supply chains, including those critical to the provision of the ‘SVO.’”

author: United24Media

text: Ukrainian military personnel placed second at international cyber exercises in Singapore.  A joint team of cybersecurity units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the 21st Signal Regiment of the United Kingdom won silver at the Defense Cyber Marvel 2026 exercises.  More than 2,500 specialists from 29 countries took part in the competition, organized by the British Ministry of Defence.  Participants practiced protecting military systems, cloud services, and critical infrastructure from complex, multi-level attacks.

author: United24Media
text: Russia has increased its military support for Iran amid the war in the Middle East, according to The Wall Street Journal.  According to the report, this includes the transfer of satellite imagery, intelligence, and components for upgraded Shahed systems to improve navigation and guidance.  In addition, Russia is advising Iran on drone tactics, drawing on its experience from the war against Ukraine—specifically on the scale of drone use in attacks and the altitudes at which they are deployed. Analysts note that Iran’s strikes have already begun to resemble Russian tactics.  Such support, although limited, significantly enhances Iran’s capabilities for precision strikes against military targets, the report says.

author: United24Media
text: 📱 “Shows the front in real time.” Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke about the iPad he gave to Charles III.  The president and Ukraine’s military leadership use iPads to track the situation on the front in real time. The device allows them to monitor large-scale attacks by Russia, control movements, and check data on enemy losses.  The president presented such an iPad to King Charles III during his visit. Similar devices are used by the prime minister, the minister of defense, and the command of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.  The head of state said the monarch asked whether he had another such device. The president replied that he only had one, to which King Charles said he would share it with Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

author: United24Media
text: “Thank you for supporting Ukraine, for being there, and for choosing to be here with us.”  This Oscar — made from the steel of a train car damaged in a Russian attack — was awarded by Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) to American actor and director Sean Penn instead of the one he was unable to receive the day before from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, having chosen to travel to Kyiv instead of attending the ceremony.  “And this award is not limited to achievements in cinema — it recognizes the resilience, humanity, and courage that keep us all moving,” Ukrzaliznytsia said in a statement.  For his part, Sean Penn, while at the capital’s train station, recited lines from Volodymyr Ivasiuk’s classic hit “Chervona Ruta” in Ukrainian.  📹: ukrainianrailways/ Instagram

author: United24Media
text: A Russian drone was found today in the Moldovan village of Tudora, believed to have been equipped with explosives. This is a serious violation of our airspace and a threat to our citizens, said Moldovan President Maia Sandu.  “Russia has repeatedly violated our sovereignty and put the lives of our people at risk.”  The Moldovan Ministry of Defence reported that the drone that crashed in Tudora, Ștefan Vodă district, was destroyed under maximum security conditions.  Moldovan experts determined that it was a Geran-2 drone. It contained explosives and posed a danger to the population.

author: United24Media
text: Russian forces dropped two FAB-250 bombs on a private sector and residential area in Kramatorsk, the City Military Administration said.  Eight people were injured in the attack, including two children.  At least three dozen private homes and two high-rise buildings were damaged.

author: United24Media
text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is on a visit to Spain, the head of state’s spokesman said.  The president is working in Madrid. He has arrived at the Sener Aerospace & Defence enterprise, where he will inspect equipment and production.  Ukrainian-Spanish defense agreements will be signed in Zelenskyy’s presence.  The visit program also includes meetings with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, the head of the Congress of Deputies Francina Armengol, the head of the Senate Pedro Rollán, as well as with King Felipe VI.

author: United24Media
text: ❗️Norway is providing $200 million in budget support to Ukraine through the World Bank’s PEACE project.  “We are deeply grateful for this timely contribution to maintaining macro-financial stability and the continuity of key public services — this is an example of Norway’s leadership and consistent support for Ukraine during a period of great challenges.  Since the launch of the program in 2022, the PEACE project in Ukraine has already mobilized almost $52 billion, of which $13.4 billion has been directed to pension payments,” Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko commented on the decision.

author: United24Media
text: A court in Poland has agreed to extradite Russian archaeologist Alexander Butyagin to Ukraine. He is wanted by Ukraine for conducting excavations in Russian-occupied Crimea. The decision can still be appealed.  Butyagin was detained in December 2025 in a Warsaw hotel during a lecture tour in Europe. Ukraine then filed an extradition request.  Russia summoned the Polish ambassador over the detention and protested against his extradition to Ukraine.

author: United24Media
text: The escalation in the Middle East has forced the world to view Ukraine differently, Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said.  Tykhyi noted that the escalation in the Persian Gulf could accelerate Ukraine’s conclusion of drone agreements and change global perceptions of the country.  According to him, Iran’s confrontation with the United States and Israel highlights Ukraine’s unique experience, making it a valuable partner.  He also referred to remarks by Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, who said that countries in the region, forced to defend themselves against Iranian drones, now see Ukraine not as a requester of aid, but as a strong military force.  Tykhy also recalled a statement by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy about Ukraine’s readiness to develop security cooperation with the United States, NATO, and other partners.

author: United24Media
text: Ukraine and Spain have signed four documents on technical and financial cooperation. In particular, agreements were reached with Sener Aerospace & Defence, which produces robotic systems, stealth drones, and components for PAC-3 missiles for Patriot air defense system.  “The agreements concern the establishment of cooperation in the missile industry and air defense. This is what will strengthen the protection of Ukrainian skies. Strengthening air defense and protecting lives is our top priority.  We discussed the possibilities of manufacturing and strengthening Ukrainian air defense. We are also interested in joint projects in the field of long-range drone production. Ukraine has new developments and is ready to scale them up,” said President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.  Sener Aerospace & Defence is a Spanish company that develops and manufactures unmanned ground logistics systems, missile components (including for the Patriot PAC-3 MSE air defense system), stealth drones, and advanced engineering solutions focused on automation and robotic systems.

author: United24Media
text: ❗️The Russian Armed Forces launched a spring–summer offensive in the Zaporizhzhia region, deploying infantry, armored vehicles, motorcycles, and even horses, according to Robert "Madyar" Brovdi.  Russian forces attempted to use fog as cover, but their reliance on “invisibility” failed — Ukrainian troops engaged the assault groups as they approached.  In the past day alone, more than 500 Russian soldiers were killed and wounded. Overall, more than 900 casualties have been reported over the past 1.5 days in the Rodinske–Huliaipole sector.  According to military reports, the enemy failed to break through the front line.

author: United24Media
text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Felipe VI of Spain at the Zarzuela Palace.  “We appreciate Spain’s assistance to our people who were forced to leave their homes because of the war. I thank His Majesty and the entire Spanish people for their unwavering support for Ukraine throughout all these years of Russian aggression,” the President said.

author: United24Media
text: Main Intelligence Directorate's (HUR) fighters attacked two Russian Project 02510 “BK-16” landing boats along with their crews while they were underway in the Black Sea.  Reconnaissance units also struck the enemy’s Valdai radar in temporarily occupied Crimea, a modern system designed to detect and counter small UAVs.  In addition, Ukrainian forces carried out precise strikes to disable:  ▪️ a radio jamming station; ▪️ a repeater for “Geran”/“Gerbera” type drones; ▪️ a complex of the “Glonass” navigation system.

author: United24Media
text: The Ukrainian Air Force released footage of combat operations against Russian drones in eastern Ukraine.

author: United24Media
text: Defenders of Kostiantynivka showed the destruction of the city under constant attacks by Russian forces.  Fighters of the 24th Separate Mechanized Brigade, who are holding the defense on the eastern approaches to Kostiantynivka, shared photos of the city, which continues to suffer daily strikes.  The city is steadily being destroyed. Aerial bombs, artillery, and drones are erasing block after block. Only the foundations remain of some buildings, the Ukrainian defenders said.  Russian FPV drones are actively targeting transport and people, including both military personnel and civilians moving around the city.  The evacuation of local residents has become almost impossible due to constant shelling of access roads.

author: United24Media

author: United24Media
text: Russians attacked the Odesa region with drones overnight, the head of the regional military administration said.  In the regional center, the strike caused destruction and fires in residential buildings across three districts.  Three people were injured.  One of the Shahed drones hit a high-rise building — several apartments, the facade, and glazing were partially destroyed. The territory of a utility company was also struck, with part of its equipment and 11 vehicles damaged. All fires have been extinguished, Oleh Kiper reported.

author: United24Media
text: Most NATO military leaders believe that Russia could attack the Alliance by 2029, said the head of the General Staff of the Czech Armed Forces, Karel Řehka.  Řehka clarified that he was not saying war is inevitable, but emphasized that it is a realistic possibility.  According to the general, to prevent such a scenario, NATO and its partners must maintain a credible deterrent, including real defense capabilities and the readiness to use them.

author: United24Media
text: “We welcome the adoption of the €90 billion loan and expect the first disbursement to Ukraine by early April,” 25 EU leaders said after the European Council meeting.  “In this context, the European Council also calls for intensified work with third countries to help cover the remaining €30 billion deficit in Ukraine’s budget,” the statement said.  Slovakia and Hungary did not join the statement. Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán again said that until the transit of Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline is resumed, Budapest will block the allocation of the loan to Ukraine and the 20th package of sanctions against Russia.  Ukraine has agreed to accept technical and financial assistance from the EU to repair the oil pipeline damaged by Russian shelling.  The day before, representatives of Naftogaz met with the EU technical working group and presented a comprehensive reconstruction plan.

author: United24Media
text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Russia must clearly understand and truly feel that Ukraine will be part of European Union and that this cannot be stopped.  According to him, Ukraine is carrying out internal reforms and working externally to secure a clear date for EU accession.  “If a clear date is set, it will mean that Russia will not be able to block our accession in any way. You see how various things are blocked and how difficult it is for a united Europe to implement even decisions that have already been made. This must not happen with the opening of clusters for Ukraine or with our accession — this is a matter of trust, security, and the future,” the President said at a European Council meeting.

author: United24Media
text: Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said that Hungary is politicizing the issue of repairing the Druzhba pipeline.  He added that instead of explaining to Hungarian citizens why the country has failed to diversify its energy supplies, Prime Minister Viktor Orbán is focusing his rhetoric on Ukraine.  “And even after the damage to the Druzhba pipeline, other Ukrainian pipelines and infrastructure have also been damaged, including the Odesa–Brody pipeline. Ukraine is repairing all this, but we do not have unlimited resources. We are in a state of full-scale war, which Hungary for some reason prefers to ignore,” Tykhyi said.

author: United24Media

The Ukrainian team — namely the political part of the negotiating group — is already on its way, and we expect to meet in the United States this Saturday,” the President said.

author: United24Media
text: The Russian army attacked an emergency medical team in the village of Hrushivka, Kupiansk district, Kharkiv region. A medic and a driver were injured.  A company vehicle was also damaged, with side windows and rear lights broken.

author: United24Media
text: A border guard from Volyn has become the European champion in jiu-jitsu.  Sergeant of the Volyn border detachment Bohdan Mochulskyi won a gold medal at the European Championship.  After the victory, Mochulskyi thanked everyone who gives him the opportunity to represent Ukraine on the international stage and raise the national flag. He also expressed gratitude to his comrades for their support and to the command for their trust, the Western Regional Department of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine reported.

author: United24Media
text: Sean Penn visited soldiers of the 3rd Operational Brigade of the National Guard of Ukraine, known as “Spartan.”  During the visit, he spoke with the guardsmen about the realities of war and expressed support for those defending independence on the front lines every day.  The brigade commander, Colonel Oleksiy Khilchenko, briefed him on the unit’s battlefield successes and presented a commemorative medal and the brigade’s battle flag.

author: United24Media
text: The “Spartan” brigade, together with adjacent units, repelled an enemy assault, destroying a Russian company within 48 hours.  The Russian occupation command committed significant forces to the attack in the Pokrovsky direction, hoping to take advantage of rainy weather. Enemy infantry attempted to advance using cars, motorcycles, and ATVs.  However, “Spartan” and nearby units stopped the attack. In 48 hours, the enemy suffered significant losses, including:  • 120 attack personnel killed; • 6 wounded.  Russian equipment losses included:  • 7 ATVs; • 4 motorcycles; • 3 cars.

Its only real lifeline is the price of oil, which is why it is so important to preserve sanctions against Russia and prevent the Kremlin from turning oil revenues into ballistic missiles.

author: United24Media
text: At night, Russian forces attacked the Zaporizhzhia district, carrying out two strikes that destroyed private homes.  A 30-year-old woman was killed, while a 48-year-old man and a 10-year-old boy were injured, said Ivan Fedorov, head of the regional military administration.

author: United24Media
text: A large convoy of trucks labeled as “Humanitarian Aid” has departed Tajikistan for Iran, drawing scrutiny amid documented defense ties between Tehran and Dushanbe and broader concerns over regional logistics networks.  The convoy raises a key question about its contents, given the lack of transparency, Tajikistan’s role in Iranian drone production, and well‑established Central Asian transit routes also used for Russia–Iran logistics.  The development has prompted comparisons to Russia’s covert military supply operations in Ukraine during the early phase of its 2014 invasion. Russia transferred weapons, ammunition, and military equipment to Ukraine's Donetsk region under the guise of humanitarian aid.

author: United24Media
text: Russian forces attacked the port of Odesa with drones overnight.  Two people were injured in the strikes.  Two civilian commercial vessels, flying the flags of Palau and Barbados, were damaged while moored at the piers and loaded with grain.  Administrative buildings, a grain bunker, and equipment were also damaged. The fires have already been extinguished.

text: Ursula von der Leyen said that Ukraine will receive €90 billion from the European Union.  “The loan remains blocked because one leader does not keep his word. But let me repeat what I already said in Kyiv. We will fulfill our promise one way or another,” the President of the European Commission said.

author: United24Media
text: Filaret, the 97-year-old Patriarch of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Kyiv Patriarchate, has passed away. He had previously been hospitalized due to deteriorating health.

author: United24Media
text: Russia is considering restricting the operation of foreign AI models, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, according to Russian media.  The official reason is to “protect citizens” from alleged hidden manipulation and discriminatory algorithms.  At the same time, services with more than 500,000 daily users would be required to store Russian citizens’ data within the country for up to three years. Chinese models such as Qwen and DeepSeek are also being considered for adaptation and use as alternatives to Western systems.

author: United24Media
text: 🦾 Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukrainian forces had foiled a Russian offensive that was planned to begin in March.  “Our guys are just great. The fact that they foiled the offensive planned by the Russians is a fact. The offensive was supposed to take place in early spring, specifically in March. The Russians failed. There were many attempts. The guys foiled it. Just great,” the President said.

author: United24Media
text: Vladimir Putin’s former translator has been appointed as an OSCE observer in the Hungarian elections, Reuters reports.  According to the publication, Hungarian human rights activists have raised concerns about the participation of Daria Boyarska in the observer mission for the parliamentary elections in Hungary on April 12.  The Hungarian Helsinki Committee called on the OSCE to remove her “to ensure trust and confidentiality.”  Boyarska is currently an adviser to the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly. She previously worked in the Russian Foreign Ministry and served as an interpreter at meetings between Putin and Donald Trump. Poland added her to its sanctions list in 2022.  VSquare journalist Szabolcs Panyi noted that Boyarska’s relatives work in structures linked to the Kremlin, which could pose risks of influence.  She declined to answer questions about the war and possible ties to Russian intelligence.

author: United24Media
text: A Russian Ka-52 helicopter was hunted down by pilots of the Baltika crew from the 1st Battalion “Predators of the Heights” of the 59th Separate Assault Brigade near Nadiyivka in the Donetsk region.  After making an emergency landing, the helicopter crew attempted to flee. Drones from the Unmanned Systems Forces then struck the area and completed the engagement, according to Robert “Magyar” Brovdy, commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces.

author: United24Media
text: ❗️Germany is temporarily simplifying arms exports to Ukraine and Gulf states to strengthen air and maritime defense.  The German Ministry of Economics said the new AGG 48 permit will be valid until September 15 and allows deliveries without prior approval for each application. It covers air defense systems and countermeasures against sea mines.  The list of countries includes Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Ukraine.  Exporters must register within 30 days of the first delivery and submit monthly export reports.

text: Oleksandr Usyk and Anthony Joshua arrived in Kyiv together.  This is the Briton’s first visit to Ukraine since the full-scale invasion began.  “Already planning a short tour of the city. I can’t wait to show you some of my favorite places!” Usyk wrote.

At the same time, enemy losses have also risen significantly: from Tuesday to Thursday alone, about 4,840 Russian troops were killed and wounded, said Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Oleksandr Syrskyi.  “The activity of overwhelming enemy forces requires us to make new, asymmetric decisions. Ukrainian troops are acting proactively, seizing the initiative and continuing to restore positions,” he said.

author: United24Media
text: Two people were killed after Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia with a Shahed drone.  A private house was destroyed in the attack. A man and a woman were killed, while two girls aged 15 and 11 were injured.

author: United24Media
text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the First Lady attended the farewell ceremony for Filaret.  “He made a great contribution to ensuring that Ukraine had its own local church. Without his perseverance and courage, it is impossible to imagine the history of Ukrainian independence, our spiritual independence, and the building of a truly strong state,” the President wrote.

author: United24Media
text: Péter Szijjártó commented on the possible relaunch of the Druzhba pipeline.  “Ukraine will run out of money faster than we will run out of oil. Therefore, after our victory in the elections, they [the Ukrainians] will be forced to launch the Druzhba pipeline, and transportation will resume on the evening of April 13,” the Hungarian Foreign Minister said.  Szijjártó also claimed that Ukraine’s membership in the European Union would supposedly bring war to Europe.

author: United24Media
text: Robert Fico said he may block an EU loan for Ukraine, following Viktor Orbán.  According to the Slovak Prime Minister, the resumption of the Druzhba oil pipeline is being hindered by Kyiv’s position, claiming that supplies were halted “for ideological reasons.”

author: United24Media
text: President Zelenskyy said that Ukraine and European countries are working to seize oil from vessels of Russia’s shadow fleet.  “While the war continues, pressure on the aggressor must also continue. We are working with European countries so that their legal frameworks allow not only stopping such vessels, but also blocking them and seizing the oil,” he said in an evening address on March 21.  Zelenskyy added that despite sanctions imposed by Ukraine, United Kingdom, the European Union, and the United States on a shadow fleet tanker detained by French naval forces, Russia continues to use it.

author: United24Media
text: The FBI said that Russian hackers have compromised thousands of accounts on messaging platforms, including Signal, according to Kash Patel.  According to the agency’s director, the campaign targeted individuals “of high intelligence value,” including current and former U.S. officials, military personnel, politicians, and journalists. The attackers were reportedly able to access correspondence, contact lists, and send messages impersonating victims.  In May 2025, investigators from Europe and the United States reported dismantling a “malicious network” linked to Russian hackers. Arrest warrants were issued for 20 suspects, most of whom are believed to be in Russia.

author: United24Media
text: In Florida, delegations from the United States and Ukraine held constructive meetings as part of ongoing mediation efforts, focusing on narrowing and resolving outstanding issues to move closer to a comprehensive peace agreement, said U.S. Presidential Special Representative Steve Witkoff.

author: United24Media
text: Border guards conducting aerial reconnaissance from the “Phoenix” unit of the “Pomsta” brigade used FPV drones to strike Russian positions.  One of the occupiers attempted to return fire but was eliminated by the drone operator.

author: United24Media
text: After Starlink was shut down for Russian forces, Ukraine has liberated the most territory in more than two years, the Wall Street Journal reports.  This has undermined Putin’s attempts to gain leverage in U.S.-brokered negotiations, the article notes.  “Ukraine’s progress since Russia lost Starlink — SpaceX’s satellite internet service — underscores how important commercial satellite internet has become in modern warfare, as well as the level of control that Elon Musk can exert over the conflict,” the WSJ writes.

author: United24Media
text: In Sumy, Russian forces struck rescuers, damaging a fire truck, the State Emergency Service reported.  “On the night of March 22, SES personnel were conducting another inspection of the area after an enemy strike.  As the rescuers were preparing to return to their unit, the enemy struck again near the fire tanker.  Fortunately, the personnel reacted in time and moved to a safe location,” the statement said.

author: United24Media
text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that in recent days, due to the easing of sanctions, Russia has increased its oil sales to finance the war against Ukraine.  According to the president, over the past week Russia has launched nearly 1,550 strike drones, more than 1,260 guided aerial bombs, and two missiles at Ukraine.

author: United24Media
text: A delegation of NATO military command led by Pierre Vandier arrived in Ukraine, said Deputy Head of the President’s Office Pavlo Palisa.  “We had a substantive discussion about involving Ukrainian forces in future NATO exercises as a hypothetical adversary (Red Team). Last year’s experience showed allies the latest methods of warfare — in training scenarios, Ukrainian units demonstrated a significant advantage.  We also discussed the future of JATEC (Joint NATO–Ukraine Center). We are entering the final stage of deploying Ukrainian control systems, developing analytical capabilities, and expanding training programs.  Today, Ukraine is not only a consumer of security — it is also a producer.  I thank Admiral Pierre Vandier and the entire delegation for the visit, openness, and readiness for practical cooperation,” Palisa said.

author: United24Media
text: India may abandon the Russian Su-57, Defense Express reports.  New Delhi is considering joining European projects such as Tempest or FCAS. The decision is based on its 2018 experience, when India withdrew from a joint program with Russia due to the aircraft not meeting requirements.  India is currently focusing on its own AMCA project and the purchase of French Rafale jets. Investments in a sixth-generation program could reach €12.5–16.5 billion, making the Su-57 economically and technologically less viable.  According to experts, such a move could significantly weaken Russia’s position in the global arms market.

author: United24Media
text: Yesterday, a Ukrainian thermal imaging company, Archer LPP, was set on fire in the Czech Republic.  A group calling itself “Earthquake Faction,” described as pro-Palestinian activists, claimed responsibility for the arson, stating its intention to target weapons production linked to Israel.

author: United24Media
text: “During the meetings, we focused on reliable security guarantees and the humanitarian track, in particular the exchange and return of our citizens. We have made progress in aligning positions and further narrowing the range of unresolved issues,” said Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council Rustem Umerov following the latest round of negotiations with the American side in Florida.  For his part, U.S. Presidential Special Representative Steve Witkoff said:  “The constructive talks built on yesterday’s progress and focused on key points for establishing a strong and reliable security system for Ukraine, as well as on critically important humanitarian efforts in the region.”

author: United24Media
text: President Zelenskyy said that Ukrainian units have already achieved concrete results in protecting Persian Gulf countries from Iranian attacks, and that Russia is irritated by the global demand for Ukrainian expertise.  He noted that “Ukraine’s experience in air defense is among the strongest in the world and is something that will ensure Ukraine remains one of the key contributors to global security after the war — among those the world will rely on to maintain security.”

author: United24Media
text: The crew of a T-64BV tank from the “Old Iron Side” unit of the 4th Operational Brigade “Rubizh” of the National Guard of Ukraine is using direct fire to strike enemy shelters in the village of Nove Shakhove, Donetsk region.

According to Center for Countering Disinformation, dozens of AI-generated videos have appeared online this year. The accounts that posted them are either bots or abandoned pages of real people.

author: United24Media
text: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that easing sanctions on Russian oil would bring Moscow about $2 billion in additional revenue, which he described as “insignificant.”  “The key question is what is better: if oil is $150 and Russia receives 70% of that — $105 — or if prices stay below $100? In that case, they earn less. Our analysis shows the maximum additional amount Russia could receive is about $2 billion, which equals roughly one day of the Russian budget,” he said.

text: The largest port on the Baltic Sea, Primorsk in Russia’s Leningrad region, was attacked by drones.  The strike caused a fuel tank to catch fire, said Governor Alexander Drozdenko. text: Ukraine’s Defense Ministry intelligence (HUR) confirmed that the UAV wreckage found on Independence Square after the March 16 attack on Kyiv was a Lancet.  “The remains of the UAV were identified as a Lancet, which may indicate that the enemy has modernized this weapon. Previously, its main purpose was to destroy vehicles, equipment, and firing positions at tactical and operational depth.  In the Lancet, the enemy is trying to implement elements of autonomous guidance using artificial intelligence modules, including solutions based on Nvidia Jetson. Similar technologies were previously detected in other enemy UAVs — V2U,” the intelligence service said.  Russia receives most of the components used to produce Lancets from abroad, primarily from the United States, as well as from Switzerland and China.  “Despite sanctions, Russia retains access to critical technologies and continues to improve its weapons. Even technological products such as modules for AI-based solutions remain available to it,” the intelligence officers concluded.
